messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma@cloudlinehealth.com>

Subject: Questions on VPC billing + pilot packaging

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Cloudline asked me to get clarity on a few items before we loop legal in:

1) Platform fee amortization: how is the platform fee applied for a 3-month pilot that we expect to scale to production within 9 months? We need a clean amortization schedule for internal CAPEX justification.
2) Support tiers: what does Premium SRE include versus Standard? Are on-call rotations billed separately?
3) Credits/discounts: would Redwood provide a pilot credit or usage buffer if we commit to a production go-live within 9 months?

We'd like the SOW and an initial price table so procurement can run numbers. Can you also confirm SOC 2 evidence and whether audit logs are retained for 12 months by default?

Attachments: none on my side yet — happy to share Cloudline's redlines once we have a draft.

Cheers,
Emma Stone
Sourcing Manager, Cloudline Health
emma@cloudlinehealth.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma@cloudlinehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on VPC billing + pilot packaging

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers below and I've attached a draft SOW and price table for your review (Redwood_VPC_SOW_v3.pdf).

1) Platform fee amortization: for pilots we typically offer two options — (A) pro-rate the platform fee monthly with an option to apply pilot fees as a credit upon production commitment within 9 months, or (B) cap platform fee during pilot and amortize remaining balance over the first 12 months of production. In the SOW I've included both models with worked examples.

2) Support tiers: Standard covers business hours ticket triage, monthly health checks, and a 12-hour initial response SLA. Premium SRE adds a named SRE, 24/7 on-call bridging (escalation during incidents), runbook pairing for the first 3 months, and two quarterly architecture reviews. On-call rotations are included in Premium; Standard can add an on-call retainer for an extra fee.

3) Credits/discounts: we can offer a pilot credit equal to one month of platform fee (applied as a billing credit) if Cloudline signs a production commitment within 9 months. For larger production commitments (>12 node-equivalent), we can structure an additional tiered discount.

SOC 2: we will provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Audit log retention: 12 months by default for hosted telemetry; for Private/VPC deployments we provide log forwarding options and can agree on retained copies for 12 months in the SOW.

Next steps: Please review the SOW and Cloudline's redlines when available. Marissa — can you review the pricing examples and propose a best-in-class concession (pilot discount + support retainer) we can offer to close this quarter?

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_VPC_SOW_v3.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Emma Stone <emma@cloudlinehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-05T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on VPC billing + pilot packaging

David —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the SOW. We reviewed the doc with finance and engineering and have a suggested path to get the pilot approved:

- Pilot structure: consumption-only pilot (metered), capped monthly platform fee of $10k during pilot (3 months). If we convert to production within 9 months, apply the one-month pilot credit plus a 10% uplift discount on the first 12 months of consumption.
- Support: we need Premium SRE for the pilot window but can't commit to a full-year retainer. Would Redwood consider providing Premium SRE for the first 3 months at no charge (to help with go-live) and then transition to a paid retainer if we go to production?
- Audit logs: we require a single canonical copy to be retained for 12 months and a mechanism to export logs on demand.

I've attached Cloudline_SOW_comments.docx with inline redlines and the procurement checklist. If you can confirm the capped fee and the premium SRE concession, we can push this to legal next week.

Best,
Emma
Attachments: Cloudline_SOW_comments.docx (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-06T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on VPC billing + pilot packaging — proposed concession plan

Forwarding Emma's redlines and procurement asks. Quick internal proposal before I respond to Cloudline:

Summary of ask from Cloudline:
- 3-month metered pilot with a $10k/month capped platform fee
- Premium SRE free for pilot (3 months)
- One-month pilot credit if convert to production within 9 months
- 12-month audit log retention and export capability

Our recommended commercial response (to close this quarter):
- Accept the capped $10k/month pilot platform fee.
- Offer Premium SRE for the first 3 months at no charge, then transition to a 6-month discounted retainer (50% of list) if they convert to production. This keeps the runway without a full-year commitment.
- Apply the one-month pilot credit on conversion.
- Confirm in SOW: 12-month audit log retention with an export endpoint and an add-on for long-term storage if requested.
- Additionally, offer a 12% discount on consumption for the first 6 months post-conversion as a sweetener (limits exposure while demonstrating value).

Risks / notes:
- Premium SRE free for 3 months is operationally heavy; engineering/sre should sign off on capacity. Grace, can you confirm we have the bandwidth for a named SRE + runbook pairing for this pilot?
- Legal: include a conditional clause tying the pilot credit and discounts to an executed production SOW within 9 months.

If we agree, I'll draft the reply and update the SOW with the capped fee, SRE concession, and the conditional conversion clause. Approve?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Commercial Deals — Redwood Inference
